hunks.baseline: Every foul odor and the reek of blood that had filled the air around him faded, and the monsters’ roars became faint echoes. But Jeok Cheongang felt none of the changes surrounding him.
hunks.sol: The foul odors and reek of blood that had filled the air faded, and the monsters’ roars became faint echoes. But Jeok Cheongang noticed none of the changes around him.

hunks.baseline: No—he couldn’t feel them.
hunks.sol: No—he couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: All his senses were already focused on a single being.
hunks.sol: All his senses were fixed on a single person.

hunks.sol: Unhurried footsteps approached through a pool of blood.

hunks.sol: The countless monsters had stopped moving and parted to either side. Between them, someone came into view, filling Jeok Cheongang’s vision.

hunks.baseline: His heart froze with a chill so sharp it hurt.

hunks.sol: The voice that slipped between his bloodless lips was more than a sound. It was a groan he couldn’t hold back, a scream he had barely managed to suppress.

hunks.baseline: “How have you been?”

hunks.baseline: A voice he had never forgotten. And a face that had grown a little unfamiliar.
hunks.sol: A voice he had never forgotten. A face that had grown a little unfamiliar.

hunks.baseline: The name of the man he was seeing again after well over ten years spilled from Jeok Cheongang’s lips with a cold breath.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang breathed out the name of the man he was seeing for the first time in more than ten years.

hunks.baseline: The man, Jangcheon, smiled faintly at his old Master.
hunks.sol: The man, Jangcheon, smiled faintly at his former Master.

hunks.baseline: Each quiet word sank into Jeok Cheongang’s ears.
hunks.sol: Each quiet word burrowed into Jeok Cheongang’s ears, raked through his lungs, and pierced his heart.

hunks.baseline: Raking through his lungs. Piercing his heart.

hunks.sol: “I was worried you might not recognize me.”

hunks.baseline: Even if a hundred years had passed instead of ten, Jeok Cheongang would have recognized him.
hunks.sol: Even if a hundred years had passed instead of ten, Jeok Cheongang would have recognized him. Then or now, however much had changed, Jangcheon was someone he could never forget for as long as he lived.

hunks.baseline: Then, as now.
Though much had changed, he was someone Jeok Cheongang could never forget—not even until his dying breath.

hunks.sol: Somewhere on an unnamed mountainside near Jeongyang in Shanxi Province, Jangcheon had died before several witnesses. Miserably, wretchedly, as though he were being judged for the many atrocities he had committed.

hunks.baseline: But.
hunks.sol: But then—

hunks.baseline: How could—

hunks.baseline: His eyes widened for a moment, then curved with a laugh.
hunks.sol: Jangcheon’s eyes widened for a moment, then curved as he let out a disbelieving laugh.

hunks.sol: “Ha. Did you think I was the kind of bastard who’d die that easily?”

hunks.baseline: “No. I definitely heard—”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s eyes wavered at the calm reply.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s gaze wavered at the calm reply.

hunks.sol: By the time he had asked around and found the place, only a few traces of the fierce battle remained. Jangcheon’s body was nowhere to be found. No one knew exactly why, and Jeok Cheongang hadn’t wanted to know.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang had only thought that the heavy snow said to have continued for nearly seven days and nights, along with the mountain beasts, might have erased Jangcheon’s last traces from the earth.

hunks.sol: “I nearly died. At the hands of that brat you’re looking after like a sacred ancestral tablet.”

hunks.sol: “I can feel a familiar power in him. The qi of our sect, the Fire Gate Clan. Once, only you and I carried it.”

hunks.sol: But the sight before him—which had to be an illusion—didn’t change. Neither the shadowed face of his former Disciple nor the voice that kept reaching his ears.

hunks.baseline: “But Master, look. I’m still alive, aren’t I?”
hunks.sol: “But Master, look at me. I’m still alive.”

hunks.sol: Jangcheon did not stop at his thunderous shout. He looked at Jeok Cheongang with eyes full of regret.

hunks.baseline: “Will you shut your mouth!”
hunks.sol: “Shut your mouth!”

hunks.baseline: “After I came back from the brink of death, I spent a great deal of time thinking about everything that had happened. A time when each day felt like ten years.”
hunks.sol: “After I came back from the brink of death, I spent a great deal of time thinking about everything that had happened. Every day felt like ten years.”

hunks.baseline: The pool of blood rippled beneath his advancing steps.
hunks.sol: The pool of blood rippled beneath his next step.

hunks.sol: Behind him, the monsters stood still as though they had agreed not to move. As Jangcheon drew closer, Jeok Cheongang could sense no danger or killing intent from him.

hunks.baseline: *That’s impossible. This is all an illusion and a hallucination.*
hunks.sol: *That can’t be. It’s all an illusion. I’m hearing things.*

hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang clenched his fists. The qi within him surged as though it had sensed its master’s turmoil, threatening to slip beyond his control. He subdued it and began to draw it up again.

hunks.baseline: Then a single unexpected sentence reached his ears.
hunks.sol: Then Jangcheon said something he had never expected to hear.

hunks.baseline: In that instant, the eyes that held the weight of a long life trembled, unlike the body that had regained its youth.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s eyes trembled. Unlike his body, which had regained its youth, they still held the weight of all his years.

hunks.baseline: “Please forgive me. No—Master, punish this wretched man yourself.”
hunks.sol: “Please forgive me. No, Master—punish me yourself.”

hunks.baseline: He mustn’t fall for this nonsense conjured by dark arts.
hunks.sol: He must not fall for lies conjured by dark arts.

hunks.baseline: And yet, for some reason—
hunks.sol: And yet—

hunks.baseline: Just as on that day when, despite having martial arts powerful enough to look down on the whole world, he could only watch his Disciple walk away.
hunks.sol: Just as it had on the day when, despite possessing martial arts powerful enough to look down on the world, he could do nothing but watch his Disciple walk away.

hunks.baseline: “I won’t make excuses. Whatever punishment you give me, I’ll bear it all.”
hunks.sol: “I won’t make excuses. Whatever punishment you give me, I’ll bear it.”

hunks.baseline: The words he had wanted to hear so badly.
hunks.sol: The words he had wanted so badly to hear.

hunks.baseline: “I betrayed your trust, disgraced our sect, and killed innocent people, committing sins that can never be washed away.”
hunks.sol: “I betrayed your trust, disgraced our sect, and killed innocent people. I committed sins I can never wash away.”

hunks.baseline: “Kill me. With the very hands that took me in more than twenty years ago.”
hunks.sol: “Kill me with the hands that took me in more than twenty years ago.”

hunks.baseline: He couldn’t breathe. His heart hurt as if an unseen hand were squeezing it.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang couldn’t breathe. His heart ached as though an unseen hand were squeezing it.

hunks.baseline: Everything he was seeing and hearing had to be nothing but an illusion.
hunks.sol: Everything he saw and heard had to be an illusion.

hunks.baseline: The wound deep inside him, the one he thought had healed, was opening again.
hunks.sol: Yet the wound deep inside him, the one he had thought long since closed, was tearing open again.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang didn’t answer.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang did not answer.

hunks.baseline: He only stared blankly at his old Disciple as his vision grew hazy.
hunks.sol: He only stared at his approaching Disciple through a haze creeping across his vision. Worn, tattered memories settled over the sight.

hunks.baseline: Along with him came the faded, tattered memories settling over the present.
Even now, more than twenty years later, he remembered it clearly.
hunks.sol: Even after more than twenty years, he remembered clearly.

hunks.sol: *“No, kill me now. With the very hands that saved me.”*

hunks.sol: *“Might Makes Right. Didn’t you teach me that, Master? That’s what Murim is—no, what the world is. The weak should die at the hands of the strong.”*

hunks.baseline: The murderer’s smile, impossible to forget.
hunks.sol: The murderer’s smile he could never forget.

hunks.baseline: *“Kill me. That’s the only way to stop me.”*
hunks.sol: *“Kill me. It’s the only way to stop me.”*

hunks.baseline: And the sight of a feeble old man, unable to stop him in the end.
hunks.sol: And the feeble old man who, in the end, had failed to stop him.

hunks.baseline: Even after he had gone out into the world to correct that mistake, he had lingered for a long time at the very spot where wild beasts and snow-laden winds had passed.
hunks.sol: He remembered going out into the world to correct that mistake, only to linger for hours where beasts and snow-laden winds had passed over the mountainside.

hunks.baseline: The mountainside where a man who had lived as Jangcheon had fallen under the name Jopil.
hunks.sol: It was the place where the man who had lived as Jangcheon had fallen under the name Jopil.

hunks.sol: A traveler, finding it strange that Jeok Cheongang still stood there late into the night, motionless as a stone monument, had asked him what was wrong.

hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang had said his only family had died there. The man had been more foolish and wretched than anyone, but Jeok Cheongang had come hoping to recover at least his body.

hunks.baseline: And in that moment, he had suddenly realized:

hunks.sol: And in that moment, he had realized that even after nearly ten years, he still wasn’t ready.

hunks.baseline: At that clear voice, the layers of memories began to scatter.
hunks.sol: The clear voice scattered the layers of memory.

hunks.sol: Tears streamed down Jeok Cheongang’s face like water through a broken dam. Through them, he saw the Disciple he had wanted so badly to meet again.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. I’m listening, Master. I’m here with you.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Your Disciple is listening, Master. I’m here with you.”

hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang beckoned to the Disciple he had finally met again. Jangcheon took the last step toward his Master’s small embrace.

hunks.sol: In the brief silence, Jangcheon’s lips parted.

hunks.sol: Hearing the agitation he could not hide, Jeok Cheongang smiled sadly.
